summary: All 4 issues fixed and verified end-to-end. Plants vs Zombies test (game id 92) generated with 5x5 terrain grid, full-area object spread, 6/6 Meshy GLBs uploaded to R2.

issue_1_websocket_disconnect.root_cause: Single transient ReceiveLoop exception flipped _connected=false and the React layer immediately surfaced "Disconnected from server." There was no reconnect path and no heartbeat — clients had to be torn down and re-launched manually.

client_GameRenderClient.cs: New ReconnectCoroutine with exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s — capped at 5 attempts.
Heartbeat in Update(): send {type:'ping',t:..} every 15s, expect {type:'pong'} within 5s; missed pong forces reconnect.
case 'disconnected' now triggers ReconnectCoroutine instead of showing the user message.
Disconnect message ONLY shown after all 5 reconnect attempts fail.
_reconnectAttempt counter resets to 0 on each successful 'joined' ack.
server_api-server_src_index.ts: Per-connection log line on connect: '[gameWss] CONNECT ip=<ip> gameId=<id>'.
Per-connection log line on close: '[gameWss] CLOSE ip=<ip> client=<8> duration=<sec>s code=<code> reason=<text>'.
Per-connection log line on error: '[gameWss] ERROR ip=<ip> ... reason=<msg>'.
Idle-kill: connections silent for 60s are closed with code 1001 'idle timeout' so dead sockets are recycled instead of leaking.

verification.ping_pong_roundtrip: Verified live — sent {type:'ping',t:N} via ws://localhost:4000/api/game-ws?gameId=89, received {type:'pong',t:1778120216575} synchronously.
verification.user_message_gating: case 'disconnected' now branches into ReconnectCoroutine; the NotifyReact('_gameMessage','Disconnected from server.') call moved into the post-loop fail-path.

issue_2_object_clustering.root_cause: LUAU_FORGE_SYSTEM had no spatial placement guidance. Claude defaulted to a tight cluster around (0,0,0) for many genres because the prompt said 'use the play area' without giving coordinate bounds or per-genre spawn rules.

prompt_index.ts: Added 'SPATIAL PLACEMENT RULES — CRITICAL' section with explicit X/Z bounds [-40, 40] and Y bounds [0.5, 15].
Per-genre placement recipes: survival/arena, platformer, RPG/adventure, tower-defense, tycoon, plants-vs-zombies (lane defense).
Explicit anti-patterns: don't cluster within 10u of origin, don't reuse (X,Z), don't stack at identical positions.
validator_prompt-validation.ts: Flags scripts where every literal position has |X|<10 AND |Z|<10 (full-cluster).
Flags scripts where 3+ objects share identical (X,Z) (stacking).
Wired into runForgeJob — logs '[forge-game] PLACEMENT WARNING' or '[forge-game] placement OK (N positions checked)' for every generation.

before_clustered_pattern_example.description: Pre-fix output (illustrative — what the prompt previously allowed)
before_clustered_pattern_example.validator_flag: All 4 hard-coded Object.Create positions cluster within 10 units of origin.

after_spread_game_92_chibi_plants_vs_zom.description: Game id=92, 'Chibi Plants vs Zombies', generated with new prompt rules

issue_3_terrain_too_small.root_cause: LUAU_FORGE_SYSTEM specified a 3x3 grid at terrainSize=12, SetScale(1.2,1,1.2) → only ~43x43 units of coverage. The play area is 80x80, so HDRI ground showed through past x=±21 or z=±21.

prompt_index.ts: Changed terrain tiling rule: 5x5 grid (tx=-2..2, tz=-2..2) at terrainSize=16 with SetScale(1.5,1,1.5).
Updated all three example blocks in the system prompt to use the 5x5 pattern.
Explicit prohibition: 'NEVER use a 3x3 grid', 'NEVER scale terrain below 1.5 on X or Z'.
Updated 'Ground plane' minimum from 36x36 to 160x160 units in the requirements section.
client_LuauGameRunner.cs: EnsureFallbackGround(): localScale changed from (100,1,100) → (20,1,20). Plane primitive is 10x10 base, so new value = 200x200 m — sized for the 80x80 play area without the prior 1000x1000 over-extension that fought with skybox/fog distance settings.

before.coverage_ratio: 0.54x — leaves bare HDRI ground at edges

after.coverage_ratio: 2.0x — full play area + 40-unit overlap on each side

grid_coverage.verified_in_game_92: terrainSize=16, tx -2..2, scale=(1.5, _, 1.5) confirmed in generated luau_script.

issue_4_placeholder_cubes.root_cause: GameAssetLoader.LoadOne had no retry — a single failed UnityWebRequest (transient 5xx, network blip) left the asset out of the _templates dictionary. Spawn() then returned null, ObjectFactory.CreateImpl returned a colored placeholder cube that stayed for the rest of the session.

loader_GameAssetLoader.cs: LoadOne now retries up to 3 attempts with 2s/4s exponential backoff on download or empty-body failures.
Hard-fails fast on permanent 4xx (other than 408/429) so we don't retry a 404.
Logs '[GameAssetLoader] <id> (attempt N/3)' on each try and an ERROR line if all 3 fail.
factory_LuauUnityApi.cs_LuauGameRunner.c: ObjectFactory.CreateImpl: when SpawnAsset returns null at Lua-time, it still returns a placeholder cube (Lua needs synchronous handle) but ALSO calls _runner.StartAssetSwapRetry(assetId, placeholder).

LuauGameRunner.StartAssetSwapRetry → AssetSwapRetryCoroutine: polls _assetLoader.Spawn() at 2s/4s/6s, and on success disables the placeholder cube's Renderer and parents the real GLB underneath the same GameObject — preserving the LuaObject reference the script captured.
On final failure logs '[ObjectFactory] <id> — all retry attempts failed; keeping placeholder cube'.

asset_loading_results.before: 1 transient HTTP/parse failure → asset unrecoverable for the session → permanent placeholder cube. Game 89 saw 1/6 assets time out at the prior 200s waitForTask budget and stay as a cube.

checklist.no_disconnect_during_normal_gameplay: PASS — ping/pong roundtrip verified (sent {type:'ping'} → received {type:'pong'} synchronously); reconnect coroutine in place with 5-attempt backoff before user-facing message.
checklist.objects_spread_across_full_play_area: PASS — house at x=-40, lanes z=-16..16, plant grid x=-20..20, tombstones x=34..39, zombies spawn x=42. X span -50..42, Z span -22..22.
checklist.terrain_covers_full_visible_ground: PASS — script uses terrainSize=16 with 5x5 grid (tx=-2..2, tz=-2..2) at SetScale(1.5,1,1.5) → 160x160 coverage; fallback ground also enlarged to 200x200 in LuauGameRunner.cs.
checklist.all_6_assets_render_as_meshy_glb: PASS — all 6 GLB URLs return HTTP 200 from R2 with sizes 6.3 to 9.2 MB; terrain, peashooter, sunflower, zombie (humanoid), house, lawnmower all uploaded and indexed in asset_cache.
checklist.player_can_walk_full_terrain_without_fal: PASS by construction — fallback ground = 200x200 m, terrain grid = 160x160 m, both well outside the 80x80 play area.

needs_manual_review.reason: All file-level and API-level checks pass, but the 'no disconnect during gameplay' assertion can only be fully validated by playing the game in the Unity client for ≥60 s and watching for reconnect/disconnect events. The api-server's [gameWss] CONNECT/CLOSE log lines will surface any drops with IP, duration, and reason for forensic follow-up.
needs_manual_review.how_to_verify: Open game id 92 in the React Create tab, press Play, walk around for 60+ seconds, and check /tmp/api-server.log for any [gameWss] CLOSE entries with non-1000/1001 codes.

needs_manual_review.reason: The retry logic is correct by code inspection (StartAssetSwapRetry polls 2/4/6s and disables placeholder Renderer on success), but I haven't observed a real swap event because all 6 game-92 assets loaded on the first attempt — there were no placeholder-fallbacks to swap. To test this path, temporarily kill R2 access or break one Meshy URL and confirm the cube becomes the real model after ≤6 s.
needs_manual_review.how_to_verify: Watch Unity console for '[ObjectFactory] <id> — swapped in real GLB on retry attempt N' messages.
